The Turkish-Crimean Invasion of Kabarda (Spring – August 1774) was a military campaign carried out by the forces of the Ottoman Empire and the Crimean Khanate against the North Caucasian principality of Kabarda. The invasion was part of the final stage of the Russo-Turkish War (1768–1774), during which the Ottoman-aligned forces attempted to reassert influence over Kabarda amid internal divisions among the Kabardian nobility and the ongoing Russian military commitments elsewhere.
Despite being outnumbered, Kabardian forces under the leadership of local nobles, supported by a Russian detachment from the Caucasus Corps, successfully repelled the invasion in a series of engagements, most notably at the Battle of Beshtamak and in the Baksan Gorge. The campaign marked the last major Turkish-Crimean military incursion into Kabardian territory before the signing of the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca in the summer of 1774.
